claims.text: Optimized annealing will refine the lamellar spacing of an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Refining the lamellar spacing by annealing will simultaneously increase yield strength and ductility relative to the as-cast state.
The initial cast alloy has relatively coarse lamellae.
The initial cast alloy has heterogeneous interphase interfaces.
Controlled annealing can improve interphase coherence while avoiding undesirable phase transformations.
Refined lamellar spacing increases interphase-boundary density.
A higher density of interfaces creates more barriers to dislocation motion.
Interface-mediated resistance to dislocation motion produces a Hall–Petch-like strengthening effect.
Reduced lamellar spacing enables a more uniform distribution of strain during deformation.
More uniform strain distribution delays localized failure and thereby enhances ductility.
Under ambient testing conditions and near-eutectic composition, optimized annealing should produce a statistically significant increase in yield strength relative to the as-cast baseline.
Under ambient testing conditions and near-eutectic composition, optimized annealing should produce a statistically significant increase in total elongation relative to the as-cast baseline.
Unwanted phase transformations can prevent the proposed simultaneous strength and ductility improvement.
Deviation from optimal eutectic proportions can prevent the proposed simultaneous strength and ductility improvement.
